A large commanded GRIPPER change overrides this: gripper 0->1 or 1->0 gives a 79-80 step chunk and the arm then actually reaches its Cartesian target. Commanding an intermediate gripper value (0.4-0.5, which the adapter latches as hold-previous) is a reliable way to buy a long chunk without changing the grasp state. Plan every transport around this. (2) The reported gripper measurement is a good empty/closed discriminator: ~0.016 = closed on nothing, ~0.99 = fully open, an intermediate value would mean holding the block. (3) Geometry: table top z=0.80, the block is a ~30 mm cube, the bowl rim ~0.85. The fingertips sit roughly 50 mm BELOW the reported eef_pos, so eef z about 0.85 already puts the pads alongside a 30 mm block; do not waste calls descending further. (4) Vision: at 224x224 the fixed front and side views are nearly useless for metric servoing here - the hand moved 50-70 mm in the world for only a few pixels of image motion, so I could not settle whether each view horizontal is world x, world y or a diagonal, and my block estimates swung between (x +0.06, y -0.02) and (x -0.04, y -0.15). Best usable cue is the wrist camera, whose image right is roughly +x and image up roughly +y at ~1 mm/px near the centre, but its frame does NOT cover the volume directly under the fingertips: the block drops out of the bottom edge once the hand is within about 5 cm of it, which is easy to misread as alignment. (5) The bowl interior contains a small stationary red marker dot - do not mistake it for the red block being placed. (6) Repeated low slides with an open gripper visibly nudged the block (its front-view pixel drifted ~18 px over the trial), so approach from above and never sweep horizontally at table level.
